shortDefinition: A method for one application to send real-time data to another application via HTTP when an event occurs.
fullDefinition: A webhook is a reverse API call — instead of an application polling for updates, it receives an automated HTTP POST request when a specific event occurs. The sending application makes an HTTP request to a URL configured by the receiving application, delivering event data in real time. Webhooks are widely used in AI workflows for event-driven automation: an AI agent can subscribe to webhooks from tools like Slack, GitHub, or Stripe to take action immediately when something happens. They enable responsive, push-based integrations that are more efficient than periodic polling.
examples: A GitHub webhook triggering an AI code review when a pull request is opened
A Stripe webhook notifying an AI assistant when a payment fails
A form submission webhook sending data to an AI categorization service
